evidence:
Pass is for this row's authored-scenario requirement, not an assertion that the configured judges have executed. Actual frozen WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks sheet row 35/check 34, says: 'If interactive/animated/responsive/themed, the judges actually click, wait, resize, or toggle — not score a still first paint.' Internal Quality Checks row 35 agrees. The frozen skill references/quality-checks.md:142-143 defines verification as whether 'the judge is told to click, wait, resize, or toggle'. Inspected every gate/scored prompt and judge file, shared context and all six public notes. Public instruction.md:7 and environment/instructions/ui.md:3,7,9 require narrow-screen use, keyboard navigation and light/dark themes; behaviour.md:5-21 additionally requires transitions, callbacks, five-second budgets, later interaction, recovery and Auto-run. No animation requirement was invented.

Both gates require actual product actions: tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 says to enter a newly authored source, 'press the app's Run control' and observe both preview and console markers; constraints/judge.toml:25-27 requires a UI save, independent clean-context load and reload. Functional prompt.md:13-17 requires observed values and elapsed times, valid pending state and batched timed actions; :113 explicitly puts timed fixtures and bounded waits in one browser call instead of comparing model replies. Its protocols cover actual example selection/edits, save/load/reload/restart/concurrent editors; S02 (:128-149) changes filenames, runs JS/HTML/CSS, clicks the live and copied handler, observes a successfully fired timer before replacing another pending timer and waits beyond its due time; S03 (:156-161) waits at least six seconds before clicking and another six before key/input, then activates Stop and tests recovery; S04 (:168-180) establishes a matching four-second callback, supersedes while pending and waits six seconds, separately Stops pending work and waits past due; S09 (:234-247) waits for termination of braced, unbraced and Promise loops and performs recovery; S10-S13 (:253-300) run failures and wait for asynchronous outcomes; S15 (:317-320) expands actual object/array controls; S16 (:326-328) runs, reads history and Clears a populated console; S17 (:334-340) measures actual automatic delay, performs closer-spaced edits spanning that delay, checks off-state and cancels a queued debounce with measured observation windows, then runs manually with Auto-run on/off; S19 (:346-348) changes actual source/filename across all three languages. S34 (:395) explicitly switches theme 'to the other appearance, then back', requires changes to chrome/editor/console, and compares preserved draft/output. S36 (:399-409) requires a working nested-timer control, a six-second nested callback beyond the original budget, ten seconds of observation, timeout feedback and recovery. The corresponding functional judge descriptors reference these protocols and do not replace them with static impressions.

Polish prompt.md:43-49 requires a real keyboard-only route from the editor through example selection and prepared saved-snippet loading back to the editor, actual key events for every enabled control and observed visible focus; pointers/programmatic focus are forbidden during that route. Polish judge.toml:23 requires editor, preview and console to be 'reached and used' at roughly 390x844; :68 activates a supported action and observes feedback. Visual prompt.md:17-22 separates visual composition from mobile usability, and :35-37 requires desktop inspection, at least two mobile surfaces at roughly 390x844 and both offered themes. Visual judge.toml:99-104 compares the same surfaces across desktop/mobile. A static first paint cannot satisfy these directions.

Verified raw evidence without using prior review verdicts. All 50 task and 34 rule-file hashes match qc/runs/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/manifest.json, and the current review policy matches its recorded hash. golden/frozen_hardening_inputs.json matches the RESULTS.json manifest_sha256; the frozen functional prompt/judge hashes, all 22 actual application file hashes and every copied driver hash also match. In golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json, facts.S03.later_interactions records waits of 6105.016 and 6104.580 ms and click/key/input counts of 1 each; completed_stop records unchanged counts after Stop and successful recovery. S04.supersede_pending records a real successful delayed-callback/error control, A pending, B started about 161 ms later, and unchanged delayed/error counts after the waiting window. S09.literal_loop_deadline records approximately 5001/5006/5002 ms termination with recovery. S17.autorun_debounce records first execution after 546.428 ms, ten edits spanning 1211.767 ms with no intermediate execution, and final execution after 550.046 ms; off and queued-cancellation evidence records 3000 ms windows, with the latter switched off about 41.346 ms after editing. S34's before/middle/after observations contain actual chrome/editor/console colour changes and restored original styles after the second click, with identical draft/preview/console state. This is supported by executed drivers/runtime_flow.cjs:35-76, workspace_flow.cjs:158-228 and :290-305. current_flow.cjs:41-48 actually runs the short nested-timer control, runs the longer callback, waits 10000 ms, checks entered/forbidden/timeout markers and recovery; its raw fact shows nested-control-done retained and shared-deadline-recovered.

Limits: this raw run is explicitly 'direct pinned Playwright', paid_provider=false, oracle_score_claimed=false; run_workflow.cjs:23 creates only a 1440x1000 viewport and :48-50 executes the functional scenario plan. Its facts/actions do not exercise the mobile resize, Polish keyboard tour or Visual both-width/both-theme presentation judgement. It also reports criterion_verdicts_produced=false and full_current_criterion_run_claimed=false. Consequently runtime support for this row is PARTIAL. No full configured judge execution, mobile/visual execution, full judge workload, Oracle score or target-model score is claimed. Those evidence gaps remain open in their runtime clearance checks; they do not reveal a missing action in the authored scenarios reviewed here.

Counterexample analysis: a plausible app that looks complete initially but only changes the theme-toggle label, expires completed handlers after five seconds, fails to restart debounce after subsequent edits, or permanently clips controls at mobile width is distinguishable by S34, S03, S17 and Polish's mobile action requirement respectively. A conforming alternative with a light initial theme, tabbed/mobile drawers, native accessible composite menus, standard undocumented Escape/Tab editor escape, hidden provisional candidate render and static restoration after Stop is explicitly accepted by app_context.md:18, functional prompt.md:17, Polish prompt.md:29-30,43-47 / judge.toml:23, and Visual judge.toml:99. These are source-level adversarial analyses, not new fixture or judge executions. No credible false-pass or false-fail defect was identified for row 34.
suggested_fix: No authored-scenario change is indicated. Before claiming execution coverage, obtain hash-bound full configured judge logs demonstrating the prescribed interactions, mobile viewport use, keyboard navigation and both-theme visual inspection; keep the existing scripted evidence labeled partial.
